Introducing XING•

XING• consists of five students from the same school who came together for the first time to join NASA Space Apps 2026. Each member played an important role in bringing our project, (Cosmic Relics), to life. IVN led the team through planning and organising while also handling coding and development. ANA and YJ focused on researching and collecting information, BONG was responsible for the design and UI/UX, while BRI handled most of the writing and project content.
summary:
Cosmic Relics

NASA's Cosmic Relics in the Silent Void

What happens to the machines, spacecraft, and equipment humanity leaves behind in space? Do their stories end when their missions are over?

Cosmic Relics is an interactive educational web experience that explores human-made objects left behind during space exploration. From historic equipment on the Moon and retired rovers on Mars to spacecraft travelling through deep space, our project uncovers the stories behind these forgotten technologies.

Through three interactive chapters — Lunar Relics, Martian Graveyards, and Deep-Space Wanderers — users can explore space hardware, discover the missions behind them, and learn about their scientific contributions. By combining historical facts, visual storytelling, and interactive features, we make space exploration history easier and more engaging to understand.

Our goal is to make overlooked space exploration history accessible to everyone, especially younger generations. We believe these objects are more than abandoned machinery; they represent humanity's achievements, discoveries, and curiosity about the universe. Through their stories, we hope to inspire future explorers, scientists, and engineers.

Because even in the silence of space, their stories deserve to be remembered.
details:
Cosmic Relics: Abandoned But Not Forgotten

NASA's Cosmic Relics in the Silent Void

1. What is the project?

  • An interactive educational website about human-made objects left behind in space.
  • Covers three environments: Moon, Mars and Deep Space.
  • Explores forgotten spacecraft, equipment and scientific instruments.

2. How does it work?

  • Users explore three main chapters:
    • Lunar Relics
    • Martian Graveyards
    • Deep-Space Wanderers
  • An interactive timeline allows users to explore important space missions.
    • Lunar Liftoff Mass Calculator.
    • Earth–Moon Laser Pulse Simulator.
  • An interactive Golden Record lets users explore sounds and messages from Earth.
  • A space glossary explains scientific terms through simple explanations and examples.

3. What can it do?

  • Commander Nova (Gemini AI): Answers users' questions about space and adapts explanations to their age group.
  • Junior Explorer (7–11): Provides simple explanations and everyday examples.
  • Cadet Briefing (12–17): Provides scientific details, equations and technical information.
  • Ghost Fleet Telemetry: Displays information about Voyager, Pioneer and New Horizons.
  • Space Soundscape: Provides different space-themed background sounds.
  • Interactive Simulations: Allows users to experiment with scientific concepts.

4. What are its benefits?

  • Makes learning about space more interesting and interactive.
  • Helps users understand complex scientific concepts.
  • Provides access to historical NASA mission information.
  • Encourages independent learning and exploration.
  • Makes space education accessible to different age groups.

5. What is the intended impact?

  • Increase awareness of humanity's space exploration history.
  • Encourage curiosity about science, technology and engineering.
  • Inspire younger generations to explore STEM subjects.
  • Help people appreciate the scientific contributions of forgotten space equipment.

6. What tools and technologies were used?

  • HTML: Website structure.
  • CSS: Website design and styling.
  • JavaScript: Website functionality and interactions.
  • SVG: Illustrations and animations.
  • HTML5 Canvas: Space and light-speed animations.
  • Web Audio API: Sound effects and audio features.
  • Gemini AI API: Powers Commander Nova.
  • Node.js and Express: Server-side functionality.
  • Cloudflare Pages: Website deployment and hosting.

7. What makes the project creative?

  • Combines space history with interactive storytelling.
  • Uses a cinematic light-speed launch experience.
  • Includes an AI astronaut that users can communicate with.
  • Allows users to experiment with scientific simulations.
  • Combines animations, sound effects and visual illustrations.
  • Provides different learning experiences for different age groups.

8. What factors did the team consider?

  • Scientific accuracy and reliable NASA information.
  • Accessibility for different age groups.
  • Simple explanations of complex topics.
  • User-friendly navigation and interface.
  • Interactive and engaging learning experiences.
  • Website performance and deployment readiness.
  • Security of the AI API key.

Our main message:

These objects are more than abandoned machines. They represent humanity's achievements, discoveries and curiosity about the universe.

Because even in the silence of space, their stories deserve to be remembered. 🚀
